name: EROA
seoDesc: EROA: work out volume flow rate (VFR) from the aliasing speed and the radius. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the aliasing speed, the radius, the maximal velocity and the velocity time integral and the EROA calculator solves for volume flow rate (VFR). Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the EROA calculator work?
sections.html:
The EROA calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports volume flow rate (VFR) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the aliasing speed (Vₐ), the radius (r), the maximal velocity (Vₘₐₓ) and the velocity time integral (VTI).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: The formula behind the EROA calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Volume flow rate (VFR)=(2 × PI × aliasing speed (Vₐ) × (radius (r) ^ 2))
EROA=((2 × PI × aliasing speed (Vₐ) × (radius (r) ^ 2)) ÷ maximal velocity (Vₘₐₓ))
Regurgitant volume (Rvₒₗ)=(velocity time integral (VTI) × ((2 × PI × aliasing speed (Vₐ) × (radius (r) ^ 2)) ÷ maximal velocity (Vₘₐₓ)))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in milliliters per second, and convertible to any of the 39 units on that chip.
  • Shown in square centimeters, and convertible to any of the 24 units on that chip.
  • Shown in milliliters, and convertible to any of the 40 units on that chip.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Speed, opening in centimeters per second
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Speed, opening in centimeters per second
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Flow rate, opening in milliliters per second
  • Area, opening in square centimeters
  • Volume, opening in milliliters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The EROA calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the aliasing speed, the radius and the maximal velocity — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the EROA calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the EROA calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns volume flow rate (VFR), derived from the aliasing speed, the radius and the maximal velocity. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the EROA calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the aliasing speed, the radius, the maximal velocity and the velocity time integral, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter aliasing speed (Vₐ) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Aliasing speed (Vₐ) opens in centimeters per second and the chip beside it offers 25 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: Is the EROA calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
